questions.question: A bag has 4 red balls and 1 blue ball. You pick one ball. Getting a red ball is...
questions.explain: The bag has both red and blue balls, so you might get either one. More red does not make it certain.

questions.question: Tomorrow, a fish will fly over your house. This is...
questions.explain: A fish cannot fly, so this will never happen. Wanting something does not make it possible.

questions.question: A jar has 5 green balls and 0 red balls. You pick one. Getting a red ball is...
questions.explain: There are no red balls in the jar, so you cannot get one. Wishing for a red ball does not make it possible.

questions.question: Maya has a bag with 6 blue crayons and 4 red crayons. She picks one without looking. Her friend says, “You will definitely get a blue crayon.” Is her friend right?
questions.explain: There are red crayons in the bag too, so you might get one. More blue does not make it certain.

questions.question: Sam says, “I really want it to snow, so it will certainly snow tomorrow in Vancouver.” Is Sam thinking correctly?
options: No, wishing does not change it.
No, it is impossible in winter.
questions.explain: Wishing for snow does not change the weather. You cannot make something certain just by wanting it.

questions.question: Leo’s bag has 2 green marbles and 8 yellow marbles. He picks one. Getting a green marble is...
questions.explain: There are green marbles in the bag, so it can happen. Unlikely is not the same as impossible.

questions.question: There are 5 cookies on the plate: 3 are chocolate and 2 are sugar. You pick one without looking. Getting a chocolate one is...
questions.explain: There are sugar cookies on the plate too, so you might get one. Wanting chocolate does not make it certain.

questions.question: A box has 7 red balls, 3 blue balls, and 0 purple balls. You pick one ball. Which statement is true?
questions.explain: There are no purple balls, so getting purple is impossible. Getting blue is possible because blue balls are in the box.

questions.question: Tom has a bag with 5 white socks and 5 black socks. He picks one. His friend says, “You will get white. It is certain because you like white.” Is the friend right?
questions.explain: There are black socks in the bag too, so you might get one. Liking white does not make it certain.

questions.question: A spinner has 2 red sections and 1 green section. You spin it. Your friend says, “Getting green is impossible because there are more red sections.” Is the friend right?
options: I want green, so it is certain.
questions.explain: There is a green section on the spinner, so it can land there. More red sections do not make green impossible.

questions.question: A bag has 9 yellow pencils and 1 blue pencil. You pick one. Your friend says, “Getting a blue pencil is impossible.” What is wrong with that?
options: Nothing is wrong with that idea.
It is certain to get blue.
Wishing for blue makes it so.
questions.explain: There is 1 blue pencil in the bag, so it is unlikely but not impossible. Calling it impossible is the mistake.

questions.question: Tomorrow is Ben's soccer game. His team will win the game. This is...
questions.explain: Ben's team could win or could lose, so the game is uncertain. Wanting to win does not make it certain.

questions.question: Tomorrow, Ana will eat her lunch on the moon. This is...
questions.explain: Kids cannot go to the moon for lunch, so this can never happen. When something can never happen, we call it impossible.

questions.question: Mia brings a snowball into a warm kitchen. It will melt. This is...
questions.explain: Snow always melts in a warm room, so this one is certain. Hoping the snowball stays does not change what happens.

questions.question: Sara has a wiggly tooth. It will fall out this week. This is...
questions.explain: A wiggly tooth may fall out this week or much later, so it is uncertain. Wishing it out does not make it sure.
